body.text: Live: Microsoft outage affects users worldwide, impacting Teams, Outlook and Copilot
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Recap
Here is a summary of the day's events:
• Microsoft reported a major outage, saying earlier this morning it was "aggressively pursuing" methods to fix the problem.
• The outage affected Outlook, Teams and Copilot.
• A later update said the problem was caused by a "large number" of servers being made "unexpectedly unavailable".
• Microsoft later said it was able to get a "subset" of servers back online and was working to apply those changes more broadly.

More updates from our most vital resource... you lot!
While many people can't use Outlook or Teams, we're still getting a steady stream of information from our comments section.
It's always really helpful to hear from you about how you are being impacted.
Your insights are important and help us - and other readers! - get a better sense of how an issue is impacting the wider community.
Our audience is the reason I'm here, tapping away at my little laptop, so it's really lovely to see so many of you chiming in.
Mimecast (if your company has access) is work as a work around to read and send emails, but functionality is limited… just fyi to share with the world. — Robert

Work in supply chain for a major supermarket. Only got teams working on mine, everything else is down. Our suppliers can't send shipping ASN to our distribution centres. Lots of trucks being turned away… — Anonymous
We can still work with our accounting software. Main downside is that we have no emails and co-pilot. It's our first test on working without AI after getting so used to it now — Leon
I can do my work without my email, but the lack of Copilot is slowing me down. Looks like I'll be doing my work the old fashion way — using critical thought! — George

As critical systems become increasingly dependent on a handful of platforms, we're creating dangerous single points of failure. Rather than trying to prevent every outage, we need to accept that failures are inevitable and focus on resilience through diversification, redundancy, and regular testing. The goal shouldn't be systems that never fail, but systems that can survive failure. — Az
Our work is ALL email! Friday the 13th sucks! However, I'm making sourdough while checking my laptop for progress updates… — Sharon
I'm receiving birthday greetings already this morning — confirming that my Outlook is up and running. BTW, I'm on the beautiful Coffs Coast. — Brian
Happy birthday to you Brian!
Which Microsoft products are down?
The list we posted earlier has grown.
Here are the services Microsoft now says are "potentially impacted":
• Exchange Online
• Microsoft Teams
• SharePoint Online
• Microsoft Copilot 365
• Microsoft Defender XDR
• Microsoft Planner
• Microsoft To Do
• Microsoft Intune
• Microsoft Defender for Office 365

• Power BI: All users may intermittently be unable to export reports with MIP sensitivity labels to PDF in Power BI.- Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center: Multiple services including Cloud Update, Cloud Policy, and Inventory.
Key Event
Microsoft says fixes have 'not provided anticipated relief' yet
It sounds as if the fixes we thought were coming from Microsoft are still a while away.
Here's what the company has said in its latest update:
"We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief.
"Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.

"To validate a potential recovery approach, we're fully isolating a portion of our service infrastructure, restarting the affected components, and gradually reintroducing traffic to confirm our services remain stable before applying this approach more broadly.
"We're also analysing traffic patterns across our entire service infrastructure and evaluating whether isolating traffic within each region may allow affected regions to recover independently."
Medical workers impacted by outage
We've heard from a few people in the medical sector this morning about how the outage is impacting them.
It sounds like there could be a few issues for workers today.
So if you're getting any kind of medical treatment or are needing to contact a medical centre today, please be kind.
We're all just muddling along, doing what we can!

I'm a psychologist and use OneDrive to keep session notes updated across the day. Guess I'm going to be working off old info now cause OneDrive is down now too. I think my clients might be missing their Telehealth appointments if they can't access their emails... - Tom
I'm waiting on a telehealth consultation and wondering if it's going to be delayed or if my GP is just running late as usual :D - Lou

Queensland Health (like plenty of other organisations, I'm sure) relies on Microsoft for email. I just came from a night shift where the emails all went out from around 4.30am... If you want to scan something into your email you're out of luck - While you don't need Outlook to give medications or treat patients, it's going to be a tricky morning trying to get referrals sent to other teams elsewhere in the hospital... - Someone else, but in Queensland

Most medical practices run off Microsoft Outlook as it’s supposed to be the safest. Thoughts and prayers to all the medical receptionists this morning. Please be kind to them and recognise this is out of their control. They are trying their best as always. - Ye old poor medical receptionist
More insights from our citizen journos
Here's another round of updates from readers who are now arriving at work.
We are family violence workers and can’t access our database which is linked to our outlook email. Super crucial for our job as all client details are held on the database. Skye

Everything is tied to email - can't even log in to other apps we use in the business to keep working on other things because 2FA comes through our email! MC

Teams and Outlook up here in far north Qld are fine. OneDrive not so good. Dan
What causes outages like this?
We've been talking this morning about how the outages have been caused by a "large number" of servers being made "unexpectedly available" all at once.
Technology journalist Leigh Stark told ABC NewsRadio's Sarah Morice that while it was not yet clear why the servers were down, it might have been caused by a cyber attack.

"If this is a security issue, I would call this a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack, which is basically when someone pretends to be millions of people all at once and it ends up basically overloading the servers and shutting them down," he said.
But as we saw with last year's Cloudflare outage, tech difficulties like this can often be caused by updates.

"When someone updates something or upgrades something in a server somewhere and doesn't fix it somewhere else, like a DNS, it often means that it can break everything else," he said. "The idea that servers are kind of built to be intelligent and software is built to be smart is a really nice notion, but most of the time it's usually leaning on the smallest thing holding them up."
"When someone updates something or upgrades something in a server somewhere and doesn't fix it somewhere else, like a DNS, it often means that it can break everything else," he said.
"The idea that servers are kind of built to be intelligent and software is built to be smart is a really nice notion, but most of the time it's usually leaning on the smallest thing holding them up."
So, what is Stark tipping the cause is?
"I personally believe this is a form of an attack rather than a hack. This has the trademarks to me of what I would call a DDoS attack, simply because we are seeing so many services go down at once."
Key Event
Microsoft working to 'accelerate recovery'
More than half an hour ago, Microsoft said it was able to get a "subset" of servers back online.
The latest update says it was applying the changes that made that possible more broadly.

"We're continuing to work through restarting and validating the affected servers to safely return them to service, and we're exploring opportunities to expedite this process. "In parallel, we're assessing whether reverting the small number of recent configuration updates we identified could help accelerate recovery."

How is the outage affecting Australians?
We've put the call out for our reporters in the field (that's you lot following along!) to let us know how the outage is affecting their day.
Here's what a few of you told us:
The outlook outage is affecting trains departing onto the network as train Consists can't be uploaded from copies sent via email — could cause delays to many services. Dan
Our organisation has Teams, no emails. Some of my co-workers who don't listen to the morning news re-started their computers because they couldn't get their emails! Kelly
On Friday the 13th as well! With productivity impacted on this kind of scale, if Albo wants to win re-election, he should declare today a public holiday. Ashley
Thankfully I can access my One Drive, so I can work, but I have no email. While disconcerting and a little frustrating, on the positive I can work now without distraction! Dunc

Work e-mail and Copilot not working, but Teams chat is working so still connected to colleagues. SharePoint is operational. Can still get work done but it just might delay progression of some things. Nothing critical though so the impact for me personally is small. A
Well, looks like I get to watch the UEFA Nations League games this morning! Go Spain! Someone somewhere
The My Telstra app is also down
My Telstra, an app that allows the company's customers to pay their bills and track their usage, is also suffering an outage.
The telco's website saying the service "isn't available right now".
"We're working hard to solve the problem and get all the great My Telstra services back online as soon as we possibly can."
The ABC has contacted Telstra to confirm if the outage is related to Microsoft servers.
How is the outage affecting you?
We want to know how the outage is affecting your day.
No matter how big or small those impacts are, chime in and keep us in the loop!
Internet outage monitor Downdetector charts Microsoft's global outage
Internet outage monitor Downdetector has released charts showing the spread of Microsoft's global outage.
Microsoft says the issues started about 5:15am AEDT and Downdetector says reports started pouring in at roughly 6:25am AEDT.
"Outlook reports alone peaked at more than 2,000 times their normal level," the service said on X.
Loading...
It said, based on its data, nearly seven in 10 reports came from inside the United States.
Downdetector has also monitored simultaneous outages at Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also to a lesser extent than Microsoft's.
"Microsoft said a portion of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions," it said.
It said at 6:38 AEDT it was receiving more than 11,000 reports of an outage each minute.
Key Event
Microsoft says some servers are back online
There's been another update from Microsoft which indicates things could be returning to normal soon.
The company says some servers are back online and it is now working to get the others back up as well.

"We've validated an alternative health check method on a subset of affected infrastructure, which allowed the servers in that subset to successfully return to service, and we're now applying this change more broadly.
"We're also preparing an automated recovery process to continually detect and restart unresponsive servers, to help keep them in service while this change progresses.
"Additionally, our review of recent changes has identified a small number of configuration updates that we're investigating as potential contributors to the issue."
It's 12 o'clock somewhere ...
It's only fairly early in the morning here in Australia, especially if you're in WA, so the outage might not be affecting a lot of people's days just yet.
But Dr Gregory says it's likely causing "absolute choas" in offices on the other side of the globe.
"Somewhere in the world it's the middle of the day and people are trying to work.
"If all of a sudden you have lost access to Outlook, you can't do your emails and you lose productivity.
"So it's a major impact across the world.
"For people in Australia, hopefully the problem will be fixed before we enter our work day.
"But it does mean that people need to be aware that there may be a slow reaction from Microsoft's Outlook suite.
"People need to look for alternative ways to connect to people, possibly pick up the phone and talk to them!"
Expert reckons a 'misconfiguration' could be linked to updates
Tech expert Mark Gregory, an associate professor at RMIT, has been on ABC News Breakfast this morning, helping us make sense of the outage.
Here's what he reckons led up to this situation:

"Microsoft announced that they were doing updates a few days ago and, as part of the update process, there's likely been a misconfiguration either in what we call BGP — which was the problem that Optus had — or another network configuration problem.
"Part of the server pool that serves the Outlook service appears to have fallen off the network.
"As we know in the Cloud, because there are so many users, possibly millions of users of Outlook, they have many different servers spread across the world that serve the users.
"They need to configure and manage all of those servers
"It appears a large number of them have essentially been dropped off the list of available servers, and so what's left can't serve all the traffic."
Which Microsoft products are down?
Quite a few of them.
Here are the services listed as "potentially impacted" by Microsoft:
• Exchange Online
• Microsoft Teams
• SharePoint Online
• Microsoft Copilot 365
• Microsoft Defender XDR
• Microsoft Planner
• Microsoft To Do
What's causing the outage?
Great question!
The company has been giving updates on Microsoft's Service Health Status website.
Earlier, it said the outage was linked to "a large number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable, which is shifting load onto the remaining infrastructure".
We're not exactly sure why those servers are unavailable, but Microsoft's team is working on it.
Here's what the company said in its latest update a few minutes ago.

"While we haven't identified any recent changes that correlate with the start of impact, our investigation indicates the failed health checks may originate from a specific component on the affected servers that's responsible for processing them.

"We're deploying a targeted change to bypass this component on a subset of servers to validate whether this restores availability, and we've taken steps to prevent additional servers from being removed from service while we work to return the affected servers to service.
"We're also investigating why affected servers are experiencing elevated processor usage while handling requests."
AI companies affected by the outage
AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic confirmed they've been affected by the widespread Microsoft outage.
ChatGPT creator, OpenAI, said it was investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors because tools were not working as expected.
Anthropic said it had identified an issue with an upstream provider affecting its Microsoft 365 connector.
Microsoft says it's working to mitigate the outage and is restarting the affected servers.
Reporting with Reuters
Widespread outage hits Microsoft platforms
Good morning. Thanks for joining us today.
If you're one of the many people having troubles accessing your Outlook emails this morning, you're not alone!
Microsoft, the company behind the email platform many people around the world rely on, is having a major outage at the moment.
Microsoft confirmed the outage was affecting Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other platforms.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," the company said.
"We're investigating what's causing these servers to become unavailable while we work to safely return them to service."
Buckle up. We'll bring you more updates as they come to hand.
